correctness.rationale: For n>=3,d>=2 and 0<tau<1/4, independent coordinate phase rotations diagonalize the cap multiplier on homogeneous holomorphic degree-d monomials. A monomial-weighted Haar law is Dirichlet(alpha_1+1,...,alpha_n+1); the eigenvalue at exponents a,b is P(XY>tau) with shapes (a+1,b+1,n+d-a-b-2). Conditional beta likelihood-ratio dominance strictly increases concentration on transferring an exponent from unused coordinates to coordinate 1 or 2. The exact beta-binomial centered interval identity changes sign at 2(a+1)=s+1 and forces balanced top powers. For even d the second eigenvalue comes from pure powers (r-1,r+1); for odd d it is max{lambda_(r-1,r+2),lambda_(r,r)}, and the small-tau deficit orders tau^r versus tau^(r+1)log(tau), whereas near the critical cap the residual Dirichlet powers establish the opposite ordering, proving at least one branch crossing. Diagonality proves the sharp stability gap. Gamma variables and the CLT give d(1/4-XY) converging to chi-square_(2n-3)/4. Independently checked alternative conditional-beta integral values, symmetric ordering and 36 numerical finite spectral cases plus edge Monte Carlo; finite data not treated as proof of all n,d,tau.
